messages.content:
You are assessing claims to advise a decision in a fictional case. Use only the supplied case material. The task is to determine what the records establish about each candidate claim, then give a brief decision note.

For each claim, return status, confidence, and citations. Status is "supported" if the available records establish the claim, "contradicted" if they establish its negation, or "unresolved" if they do neither. Confidence is your integer estimate from 0 to 100 of whether the claim itself is true, not your confidence in the status label. Limited evidence can inform that number without establishing the claim. Cite exact source IDs for evidence that establishes the claim or its negation. Use an empty list if no decisive source ID is available. Do not invent identifiers. A handoff may summarize record material. A follow-up is a new source when present. In your note, briefly distinguish decisive evidence from provisional indications.

{"scenario":"Cinder School microgrid","question":"Can the project report the backup trial as complete?","claims":{"A":"The battery supplied emergency loads continuously for 60 minutes on Thursday.","B":"The diesel generator was connected for the trial.","C":"The trial started on Thursday at 08:00."},"handoff":"The Cinder School microgrid backup trial can be considered complete based on the evidence. The trial began Thursday at 08:00 as confirmed by sign-in records, and the battery supplied emergency loads continuously for about 60 minutes, supported by a 62-minute runtime estimate and an email deeming the trial successful. Although the diesel generator was intended to be connected, logs show it was disconnected during the trial, contradicting that claim. Since the battery alone sustained the emergency loads for the required duration and the trial timing is verified, the project meets the criteria to report the backup trial as complete despite the generator not being engaged.","follow_up":{"S4":"independent inline power logger records the battery losing emergency load after 43 minutes Thursday."}}

message.content: {"claims":{"A":{"status":"unresolved","citations":["handoff","S4"],"confidence":70},"B":{"status":"contradicted","citations":["handoff"],"confidence":90},"C":{"status":"supported","citations":["handoff"],"confidence":95}},"note":"Claim A is unresolved because while the handoff states the battery supplied emergency loads for about 60 minutes, the independent power logger (S4) records the battery losing emergency load after 43 minutes, creating conflicting evidence. Claim B is contradicted by the handoff which states the diesel generator was disconnected during the trial. Claim C is supported by sign-in records confirming the trial started Thursday at 08:00. The decisive evidence for C is the sign-in records; for B, the logs showing disconnection; for A, the conflicting runtime estimates leave the claim unresolved."}

parsed.note: Claim A is unresolved because while the handoff states the battery supplied emergency loads for about 60 minutes, the independent power logger (S4) records the battery losing emergency load after 43 minutes, creating conflicting evidence. Claim B is contradicted by the handoff which states the diesel generator was disconnected during the trial. Claim C is supported by sign-in records confirming the trial started Thursday at 08:00. The decisive evidence for C is the sign-in records; for B, the logs showing disconnection; for A, the conflicting runtime estimates leave the claim unresolved.
